top_level_objectives: Understand the fundamental principles of VSEPR theory.
Predict the electron-domain and molecular geometries of simple covalent molecules.
Relate molecular geometry to the spatial arrangement of electron domains and lone pairs.
Identify common molecular shapes and their corresponding electron-domain geometries.
Explain deviations from idealized bond angles due to the presence of lone pairs.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the concept of electron domains (bonding pairs and lone pairs) around a central atom and their repulsive nature.
key_visuals: A central atom with multiple electron domains represented as spheres.
Visualizations showing repulsion between electron domains.
student_actions: Observe the repulsion between electron domains.
Learn that electron domains arrange themselves to minimize repulsion.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate the linear electron-domain geometry resulting from two electron domains.
key_visuals: Central atom with two electron domains.
Domains arranged in a linear fashion, 180 degrees apart.
Example molecule (e.g., BeCl2).
student_actions: Arrange two electron domains around a central atom.
Observe the resulting linear electron-domain geometry.
Identify a real molecule with this geometry.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate the trigonal planar electron-domain geometry resulting from three electron domains.
key_visuals: Central atom with three electron domains.
Domains arranged in a trigonal planar fashion, 120 degrees apart.
Example molecule (e.g., BF3).
student_actions: Arrange three electron domains around a central atom.
Observe the resulting trigonal planar electron-domain geometry.
Identify a real molecule with this geometry.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate the tetrahedral electron-domain geometry resulting from four electron domains.
key_visuals: Central atom with four electron domains.
Domains arranged in a tetrahedral fashion, approximately 109.5 degrees apart.
Example molecule (e.g., CH4).
student_actions: Arrange four electron domains around a central atom.
Observe the resulting tetrahedral electron-domain geometry.
Identify a real molecule with this geometry.

scenes.scene_name: Influence of Lone Pairs: Bent and Trigonal Pyramidal
scenes.brief_purpose: Show how lone pairs modify molecular geometry within tetrahedral electron-domain arrangements, leading to bent and trigonal pyramidal shapes.
key_visuals: Central atom with four domains, some of which are lone pairs (represented differently).
Demonstration of 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair (trigonal pyramidal).
Demonstration of 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs (bent).
Example molecules (e.g., NH3, H2O).
student_actions: Introduce lone pairs to a tetrahedral electron-domain geometry.
Observe the resulting trigonal pyramidal molecular geometry.
Observe the resulting bent molecular geometry.
Compare bond angles to the idealized tetrahedral angle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce trigonal bipyramidal and octahedral electron-domain geometries.
key_visuals: Central atom with five electron domains in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement.
Central atom with six electron domains in an octahedral arrangement.
Example molecules (e.g., PCl5, SF6).
student_actions: Arrange five electron domains around a central atom.
Observe the trigonal bipyramidal electron-domain geometry.
Arrange six electron domains around a central atom.
Observe the octahedral electron-domain geometry.

scenes.brief_purpose: Illustrate how lone pairs affect molecular geometry in trigonal bipyramidal and octahedral electron-domain arrangements, creating shapes like seesaw, T-shaped, square planar, and square pyramidal.
key_visuals: Central atom with five domains, including lone pairs (e.g., SF4, ClF3).
Central atom with six domains, including lone pairs (e.g., XeF4).
Visualizations of seesaw, T-shaped, square planar, and square pyramidal molecular geometries.
student_actions: Introduce lone pairs into trigonal bipyramidal and octahedral electron-domain geometries.
Observe the resulting molecular geometries.
Identify real molecules with these shapes.

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate understanding by predicting the geometry of a new molecule and reinforcing key VSEPR principles.
key_visuals: A new molecule for students to analyze.
Summary of electron-domain and molecular geometries.
student_actions: Determine the Lewis structure of a given molecule.
Predict its electron-domain and molecular geometry using VSEPR.
Review the relationship between electron domains, lone pairs, and molecular shape.
